name: yoinks
short: Download a video from a link in your terminal, without ad-filled sites.
what: A terminal app where you paste a video link, pick a resolution or MP3, and it saves the file to your Downloads folder. The README says it works with YouTube, X, Instagram, Threads, TikTok and over 1,800 other sites.
who: Anyone happy to type one command in a terminal who's tired of ad-filled downloader websites. It isn't an AI tool.
needs: Nothing else. It downloads yt-dlp for you on first run, and uses ffmpeg if you have it (with a built-in fallback)

try.label: From the README
try.text:
yoinks <video link>

Or run yoinks on its own and paste a link when it asks. Pick a format with the arrow keys and press Enter. Esc goes back, Ctrl+C quits.

watch: The README says downloading can break a platform's terms of service. Only download what you have the right to keep.
Files always go to your Downloads folder. There's no option to change it yet, and playlists aren't supported.
The yt-dlp it downloads doesn't update itself yet, so sites may stop working over time. If you already have yt-dlp installed, yoinks uses yours.
